governing_rule: Tracks retain domain-specific units and claim ceilings. Do not compute or publish a pooled score, scalar trust score, or universal assurance level.

tracks.name: Time-qualified dependency hypergraph
tracks.current_evidence: The earlier isolated Rust reference workflow passed at an earlier head. The 12-case public pack is now supplemented by eight metamorphic Rust tests and a separate Go standard-library verifier. The latest exact-head Rust/Go workflows are pending; broad Mycelix CI is skipped for the isolated-tools change.
tracks.fixture_state: 12 frozen public cases plus eight metamorphic properties: ordering invariance, domain noninterference, half-open time boundaries, incomplete-inventory monotonicity, preservation of known common ancestors under uncertainty, and shared-edge insertion/staleness behavior. The public cases are not blind hidden-truth evaluation.
tracks.claim_ceiling: Declared common-dependency assessment over an exact inventory snapshot and evidence frontier; not proof of physical or statistical independence.
next_work: Complete exact-head Rust and Go compilation/test/Clippy workflows.
Add sealed evaluator-owned hidden-truth scenarios with withheld common-cause edges and outcome schedules.

Measure 10, 100, 1000 and 10000 source scales, and report node/edge density with p50/p95/p99 runtime and peak memory.

tracks.name: Defeater-aware executable assurance case graph
tracks.current_evidence: An isolated Rust evaluator models claims, arguments, context, assumptions, evidence, defeaters and rebuttals. It uses strict input/report schemas, exact-byte SHA-256 binding, bounded evidence validity, dependency-admissibility checks, exact-target fresh rebuttals and indexed graph validation. The branch currently contains 33 adversarial/property Rust tests plus a 25-ID registry and a scale harness for 10, 100, 1000 and 10000 evidence nodes. Exact-head CI has not yet executed the final branch head.
tracks.fixture_state: Public synthetic software conformance: 25 frozen case IDs, 33 adversarial/metamorphic tests and a four-point scale harness. Includes argument-level assumption/defeater propagation, fresh/stale rebuttals, shared/unknown dependencies, physical-independence overclaim, inventory incompleteness, invalid graph controls, exact-byte binding and schema checks.
tracks.claim_ceiling: Graph-structure and declared evidence-obligation evaluation for a synthetic case. No proof of evidence truth, signature authentication, organizational independence, premises truth, safety certification or regulatory conformity.
next_work: Complete exact-head format, compile, 33-test, schema, scale-harness and Clippy gates; repair any failures.
Record actual p50/p95/p99 and process peak-RSS measurements for 10, 100, 1000 and 10000 evidence nodes.
Add generated property-based graphs and mutation testing, including orphan/unbound evidence and argument-path defeaters.
Add independent evaluator-owned blind cases and custody/access-monitor evidence; do not treat public tests as blind evaluation.
Integrate authenticated source and custody receipts through existing owners without introducing another trust root.

tracks.name: Hidden common-cause discovery through controlled intervention
tracks.current_evidence: An isolated Rust package separates a public-only candidate evaluator from hidden-truth scoring. It models active/sham interventions, per-endpoint response contrasts, explicit negative-control channels, event-time/receive-time, clock-mapping quality, missing observations, sham nuisance and hidden causal paths. The public suite contains 13 adversarial/property tests, strict input/report/truth/score schemas, and public common-cause, sham-nuisance and synchronous-independent controls. Exact-head CI has not yet qualified the latest head.
tracks.fixture_state: 13 named public synthetic software-conformance cases. Public fixtures are separate from hidden-truth examples. Includes common-cause positive, no-path negative, sham nuisance, explicit negative-control collector artifact, missing observation, unknown/invalid time mapping, delayed receive time, false non-detection, false-positive synchronous unrelated faults, stale report binding, hidden topology commitment mutation and duplicate observations.
tracks.claim_ceiling: Synthetic intervention/observation semantics and hidden-topology scoring under a declared intervention envelope. Non-detection does not establish physical/statistical independence. No arbitrary causal discovery, field failure probability, evaluator-custody authentication, PNT/telecom qualification or safety certification.
next_work: Complete exact-head formatting, Rust compilation, schema tests, 13-case registry, adversarial tests, candidate CLI smoke and Clippy.
Add evaluator-held hidden truth outside the candidate repository and authenticated schedule/custody receipts using the sealed-evaluation owner.
Add multi-domain interventions for GNSS antenna/reference, oscillator, power, network, correction provider, firmware and antenna-site causes.
Add nuisance controls for shared collectors, adapters, clocks and environmental channels; publish confidence bounds per domain.
Add safe active-experiment planning (EMSR-ACTIVE-001 / Mycelix #5984) using minimax hypothesis separation within a declared safety envelope.
Report p50/p95/p99 detection latency and scale by endpoint count, trial count and causal-path depth; then run hardware-in-the-loop replications.

external_comparators.comparison_rule: Keep dataset/protocol rows separate. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced and not directly comparable to Luminous runs until acquisition, split, label and evaluator protocols are matched.
external_comparators.limitation: Curated protocol results do not establish broad industrial emitter generalization or physical RF acquisition qualification. The reported WiSig ManyTx open-set macro-F1 (84.16%) is only 0.11 percentage points above the paper's max-similarity-threshold baseline (84.05%); the paper notes incomplete paired per-seed records and makes no formal paired significance claim for its main tables, so do not represent this small margin as a statistically established win.
